methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $103M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Equilibrium Energy is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Ryan Hanley and Alvin Henrick that has raised $103M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 3 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies (KoBold Metals at $3.0B Series C, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B Series C, and Amogy at $700M Series C), alongside 1 public comparable and 8 additional private references in the climate tech ecosystem.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy base and applying a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yields $196M. Peer-median analysis across the 3-company comp set—with a range of $700M to $3.0B—produces $1.0B as the median implied valuation. The disparity reflects the wide stage and outcome variance within climate tech; peers at Series C command substantially higher valuations than Equilibrium's current stage position would suggest.

Triangulating these methods produces a valuation range of $166M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $598M. The wide dispersion reflects genuine uncertainty around Equilibrium's technology readiness, capital efficiency relative to peers, and path to Series C funding. Stage-progression offers a floor anchored to capital deployed; peer median offers a ceiling informed by recent comparable transactions. The $598M midpoint suggests Equilibrium likely values between early stage-progression momentum and peer median benchmarks.
